what: Rows returned by the statement printed by `node outbox/venue-review-counts-2026-11-12.mjs sql 2026-07-01 2026-11-11`, run on D1 database field-archive (cc49101c-0569-4d41-8e7a-be139cde4f26) through the D1 connector on 2026-11-12. Saved BY HAND from the connector's output (the connector returns rows to the session, not to a file), so `report` and `selftest` refuse them unless they check out mechanically: see `analyze` in the script. Read-only SELECT; the connector reported changed_db false. An earlier version of the statement (six compound terms, 3655 bytes, sha256 c3248cee8a9e78d1de06d9f04d88783e624cf4464bcde99c5a3c71dc9ed32bad) was refused by D1 with `too many terms in compound SELECT` before it ran; the statement these rows came from is the five-term rewrite.

ddl.what: The two tables' definitions, read from sqlite_master through the same connector on 2026-11-12 (read-only, changed_db false), so that `s.venue = rv.n` can be said to compare bytes: SQLite uses the column's collation, and BINARY is the default only if no COLLATE clause is declared. The WHERE clause returns every table of the two names and any object, of any type, whose definition mentions COLLATE; only the two tables came back. Saved by hand; `checkDdl` in the script refuses this record if either table lacks a `venue TEXT` column line, carries COLLATE, or if any non-table object came back.
ddl.sql: SELECT name, type, sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE tbl_name IN ('regular_season_games', 'postseason_games') AND (sql LIKE '%COLLATE%' OR type = 'table')
